assertionResults.title: Threshold and false-positive controls update economics live

steps.action: Open http://localhost:3501/projects/target-shrink and capture the initial control panel plus threshold economics strip.
steps.expected: Current threshold, recommended threshold, and economics values are visible before interaction.
steps.observed: Visible baseline values were: Detain threshold 85%, False-positive cost multiplier 100%, Current threshold 85%, Expected net value -$2K, Recommended threshold 85%, Triggered incidents 3. The threshold economics strip also showed Monthly net economics signal -$7K and the note '85% remains the frontier argmax and the live stop rule is aligned with it.'

steps.action: Lower the detain threshold seven ArrowLeft steps and raise the false-positive multiplier eight ArrowRight steps.
steps.expected: Threshold and false-positive assumptions change through the route controls without leaving the page.
steps.observed: The controls updated live to Detain threshold 78% and False-positive cost multiplier 108%.

steps.action: Inspect the same visible control-panel and recommendation outputs after the control changes.
steps.expected: Either the recommended-threshold output recomputes, or the UI explicitly explains that the recommendation stays unchanged while economics update.
steps.observed: The page recomputed economics and also added explicit unchanged-recommendation labeling. After the control change, the visible outputs became: Current threshold 78%, Expected net value -$3K, Triggered incidents 4, Recommended threshold 85%. The recommendation copy changed to '85% remains the frontier argmax even at 108% false-positive cost. Economics moved, but no alternate cutoff beats it yet.' The threshold economics strip also updated to 'MONTHLY NET ECONOMICS SIGNAL -$10K' and '85% still maximizes recovered net under the active assumptions; the live 78% threshold is currently off the frontier optimum.'

evidence.network: No additional XHR/fetch requests were captured; the threshold and economics updates appeared in-page on the existing route.

frictions.description: Raw body-text capture on this Next.js App Router page included streamed payload/script text, which made unfocused text dumps noisy.
frictions.resolution: Used screenshots plus targeted in-browser extraction of the visible threshold/economics sections to capture exact before/after labels and values.

summary: Re-tested VAL-SHRINK-002 on the production-like Target Shrink route. The assertion now passes: changing the threshold and false-positive assumptions updated current-threshold and economics values live, while the UI explicitly stated that the recommended threshold remained 85% because it was still the frontier argmax under the new assumptions.
